Default question sets for validate_repeated_entries()

ck_repeated_entries_sections.Rd

Returns the three looped question sets of the 4Mi XLSForm that validate_repeated_entries checks by default. Use it as a starting point when your tool numbers the questions differently: change, add or drop sets and pass the result to the sections argument.

Usage

ck_repeated_entries_sections()

Value

A named list of question sets.

Details

Each set is a list with:

label

Name used in the issue message, e.g. "Main stops".

item

What one entry is called in the issue message, e.g. "stop" gives "stop 2 (Q59/Q60)".

slots

A list with one named character vector per entry, in the order they are asked. Every slot of a set must have the same length and its columns in the same order, so the columns of one entry can move into the entry above it.

scope

"adjacent" (the default) compares each entry with the one straight before it. "any" compares it with every earlier entry, so the same location cannot appear twice anywhere in the loop.

country_lists, place_lists

Optional. Names of the XLSForm choice lists the country and place questions use. With tool_choices, typed "Other" answers are matched against every label of these lists, in every language of the form.

place_filter

Optional. The choices column that links a place to its country (the choice_filter column), "cf" in 4Mi.

The names inside a slot decide which columns are compared:

country

Required. The country question. An entry whose country is blank or one of stop_values ends the list.

place

Optional. When present, an entry only counts as a repeat if both country and place match.

country_other, place_other

Optional. The "please specify" answer. It is compared too, so two "Other" answers only match when what was typed or picked matches.

Columns without a name (e.g. why_stop, risks, perpetrators and their "please specify" texts) are not compared but move with their entry. Select-multiple sub-columns (Q58/1, Q58/2, ...) are found automatically and move with their parent column.

The defaults are:

countries_transited

Q47 to Q54, compared on country, next to each other only.

main_stops

Q56 to Q70 in five blocks of country, place and why_stop, compared on country + place, next to each other only.

dangerous_locations

Q98 to Q117 in five blocks of country, place, risks and perpetrators, compared on country + place across the whole loop. Q98/Q99 is the first dangerous location.

A journey can pass through the same country or stop twice, so countries and stops are only checked next to each other. A dangerous location should only be listed once.

Examples

sets <- ck_repeated_entries_sections()
names(sets)
#> [1] "countries_transited" "main_stops"          "dangerous_locations"

# run only the countries transited check
sets <- sets["countries_transited"]
